item.description:
New

  • Settings ▸ Licence shows how many of your five Macs are using your licence. Deactivate this Mac frees its place for another one.
  • Export every version of a photo, not just the live one. Tick Include all versions and each one writes its own file, named after the version it came from.
  • Put back an earlier copy of a folder's edits. File ▸ Earlier Copies of This Folder… lists what Chili RAW has kept for it, so a change you regret can be walked back one folder at a time.
  • A backup drive that would silently lose your edits is caught before you rely on it. Some drives and sync folders quietly discard them when you mirror your photos, and the Backups settings now say so.
  • Restore from a backup. Pick one, confirm, and your edits, presets, albums, Looks, LUTs, watermarks, named faces and photo folders come back — your photo files are never touched.
  • Look inside a backup before you need it. File ▸ Look Inside a Backup… shows what a backup holds — your edits, named faces, presets and albums — and flags any photo folder that is not on this Mac.
  • The full right-click menu, everywhere a photo is — the filmstrip in Develop, Pixels, Compare and the Lightbox, and the Lightbox photo itself.
  • Arrange the Develop panel your way. Drag a section by its header, or right-click it to move it. Edit and Grading each keep their own order.
  • A watermark on export. Text or a PNG on every copy a batch writes, in one of nine positions, previewed before it runs.
  • A border round your photos on export — any thickness, in white, black or grey. Pro adds 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 shapes.
  • Frames in Pixels, in the photo's own colours. A Mount grows the canvas around the picture rather than painting over it, and survives an export.
  • Switch a RAW+JPEG pair with one click. A corner badge says which file you are looking at; click it for the other one. Each keeps its own edits.
  • Chili RAW is in the Shortcuts app — export with a preset, apply a develop preset, set a rating, set a flag. Pro.

Changed

  • The Neutral tone mode is now called Minimal, and it now lives up to it. It adds no look of its own, so a film Look or a LUT starts from a clean image — at the cost of highlights that clip rather than roll off.
  • The People mask is now called Person. The People view, where you name faces, is unchanged.
  • Generative Remove no longer appears when a Person mask is narrowed to a face part. Erasing someone's lips or eyes was never a useful edit; it stays for Whole person.
  • The mask panel no longer explains Generative Remove at length. The button is where it was, with the sliders back in easy reach under it.
  • Film Labor's Grain slider reaches much further. What used to be full strength sits about a third of the way along it now, so grain shows where it was barely there before.
  • The Film Labor picture is sharper on a large window, and grain there now reads the way it does in an exported file.
  • Zooming into the Film Labor picture shows real detail. Past Fit you now see the grain your file will have, rather than a magnified version of the small one.
  • A film stock now arrives at 75 % strength rather than full, on a Look slider that is longer than it was, so small adjustments are easier to make.
  • The Film Stock swatches are gone from the Grading panel. LUTs are now the one place for a film look — import a .cube of your own, or link a folder of them.

Fixed

  • A Person mask's Hair no longer stops in a straight line across the photo. Long hair is now masked to its ends, and Neck and Clothing reach as far as they need to.
  • Thumbnails keep filling in while you edit. In a folder of edited photos the filmstrip and the grid used to stop on grey placeholders for seconds at a time.
  • Turning on lens corrections no longer closes the app. Ticking Enable Profile Corrections in Develop ▸ Geometry now reads the photo's built-in correction data without interrupting the panel.
  • The filter band lays out properly in a narrow window. The count and its two buttons drop below the filters instead of squeezing them into a corner, the columns spread to fill each line, and the number of photos shown no longer breaks across two lines.
  • Develop tabs remember where you were. Geometry opens at the top the first time instead of part way down, and after that each tab comes back to the spot you left it.
  • A backup that fails now says so, and names what it couldn't copy — with a Copy Details button in Settings ▸ Backups for the full list.
  • A failed backup no longer replaces the one you already had. Backing up twice in one day, with the second attempt failing, used to leave you with neither.
  • Renaming the backup subfolder no longer doubles your library, or empties it when a folder above your photos happens to share the name.
  • The hidden safety copies no longer pile up. Each is removed once the write it protects is confirmed good, instead of staying on your drive for ever.
  • The safety-copy folder can no longer be renamed. A name you already chose keeps working.
  • Two photo folders with the same name both make it into a backup. Only the first used to; the second's edits were left out without a word.
  • Old backups are cleared away. The ten most recent dated backups are kept and older ones removed, instead of one building up per day for ever.
  • A backup now carries every face you have named. Detection can find the faces again, but never who they are.
  • A backup now carries your export presets, your watermarks and your photo folders, so a restore gives back the export side of the app too.
  • The restore notes inside a backup now cover everything in it — the catalog and your edits, not only the app's own settings — and say how to put each piece back.
  • A film look no longer flattens the brightest parts of a photo. The sun, a lamp or a bright reflection kept its shape instead of turning into a flat patch of sky.
  • Print Character now relaxes the paper instead of darkening the picture. Turning it down used to deepen the shadows; it opens them.
  • Renaming several photos at once no longer empties the folder.
  • A renamed photo keeps everything you gave it — its people, its film look, its collections and its RAW+JPEG side choice.
  • A launch can no longer stall on a blank screen.
  • A chosen crop ratio now holds while you drag.
  • A cropped photo fills the Develop canvas again.
  • A backup now carries your imported LUTs, your starred LUTs and your saved Looks, along with the folder you linked them from.
  • The histogram follows a clip while it plays instead of freezing on the frame you started from.
  • Darkroom (⌃⌘F) now clears the whole screen, Develop panel and filmstrip included, and takes the window full-screen. ⌃⌘F again brings it all back.
  • Switching folders with a filter on no longer closes the app. Filtering the grid and then clicking another folder in the sidebar could quit Chili RAW.
